UnitStatement: The solver diagnostics crate turns mechanics-solver findings into deterministic diagnostic records; it does not encode design-code checks, professional approval, protected standards content, or private project data.
DiagnosticSeverity enum defines four severity levels: Info, Warning, Blocking, and Failure.
DiagnosticSource enum identifies the origin of a diagnostic: ModelValidation, MechanicsSolver, SolverConfiguration, or SolverIteration.
DiagnosticSource maps to an analysis-boundary source string: ModelValidation yields 'model_validation'; MechanicsSolver, SolverConfiguration, and SolverIteration all yield 'mechanics_solver'.
SolverDiagnosticClass enum classifies diagnostics as SolveBlocking, AssumptionWarning, NonlinearWarning, or Tbd.
SolverDiagnosticClass maps to analysis-boundary class strings SOLVE_BLOCKING, ASSUMPTION_WARNING, NONLINEAR_WARNING, and TBD.
DiagnosticProvenance records source_name, source_location, source_license, contributor, redistribution_status, and review_status for a diagnostic.

DiagnosticProvenance::solver_generated produces provenance with source_name 'OpenPipeStress solver diagnostics', license 'project-governed', contributor 'software', redistribution 'public_project_record', and review_status 'TBD'.
SolverStatus enum defines solve states: ReadyToSolve, MechanicsSolved, SolvedWithWarnings, ModelIncomplete, and SolveFailed.

SolverStatus maps to an analysis boundary mapping; ReadyToSolve/ModelIncomplete/SolveFailed map to MODEL_INCOMPLETE, while MechanicsSolved/SolvedWithWarnings map to MECHANICS_SOLVED, always with mechanics_authority 'solver_result_only' and human_review_required true.
The analysis boundary mapping never emits rule status or human acceptance (emits_rule_status=false, emits_human_acceptance=false); the solver result carries no human or rule authority.

AnalysisBoundaryStatusMapping struct carries mechanics_status, automatic_status, mechanics_authority, human_review_required, emits_rule_status, emits_human_acceptance, and status_evidence_ref_required.

SolverDiagnosticCode enum enumerates diagnostic codes: SingularSystem, IllConditionedSystem, ConditioningFailure, InvalidRestraint, InvalidModelTopology, InvalidNumericInput, NonConvergence, NonPositivePivot, SparseSolverTbd, and TolerancePolicyTbd.
SolverDiagnostic struct holds code, class, severity, source, message, optional affected_ref, optional canonical_ref, optional remediation, provenance, and quantity_units.
SolverDiagnostic::new derives the diagnostic class from code/severity/source, sets default remediation, and stamps solver-generated provenance for 'core/solver/diagnostics'.
A SolverDiagnostic is_blocking when its severity is Blocking or Failure.
SolverDiagnosticReport holds a SolverStatus plus a vector of SolverDiagnostic; is_blocked is true if any contained diagnostic is blocking.
DiagnosticsError enum covers NonFiniteInput, NegativeInput, and InvalidThresholds error conditions for diagnostic computation.
Conditioning thresholds must satisfy 1.0 <= warning <= failure; otherwise an InvalidThresholds error is returned.

diagnostic_from_frame_error maps each FrameKernelError variant to a SolverDiagnostic with appropriate code, severity, and source (e.g. SingularSystem -> Failure/MechanicsSolver; restraint and topology errors -> Blocking/ModelValidation).
report_frame_error builds a SolverDiagnosticReport with status SolveFailed containing the single diagnostic mapped from the frame error.
diagnostic_from_linear_support_error maps a LinearSupportError to a Blocking InvalidNumericInput diagnostic sourced from ModelValidation.
diagnostic_from_support_finding maps a SupportFinding to a Blocking ModelValidation diagnostic, attaching the support_id as the affected_ref.
diagnostics_from_support_application_error converts a SupportApplicationError into one or more diagnostics, including DOF-alignment and out-of-range restraint cases.
diagnostic_from_primitive_load_error and diagnostic_from_primitive_load_finding map primitive load errors and findings into Blocking ModelValidation diagnostics.
classify_condition_ratio returns a Failure ConditioningFailure diagnostic when ratio >= failure_threshold, a Warning IllConditionedSystem diagnostic when ratio >= warning_threshold, otherwise None.
convergence_diagnostic returns None when residual_norm <= tolerance; a Failure NonConvergence when residual exceeds tolerance at the iteration limit; otherwise a Warning NonConvergence.

The sparse solver selection is resolved by human ruling DEC-023 (D-03 Option C: in-repo skyline LDL^T direct solver, core/solver/sparse_direct); binding the live product solve path to that solver remains TBD, so the dense solve path stays live.
sparse_solver_tbd_diagnostic emits a Warning SparseSolverTbd diagnostic stating DEC-023 resolved the sparse solver but live solve-path adoption remains TBD.

diagnostic_from_sparse_error maps a SparseDirectError; a singular pivot is reported with both its profile-ordered location and the original pre-ordering reduced index so the failure traces back to a model degree of freedom.

diagnostics_from_factorization_report maps a completed sparse factorization report into deterministic diagnostics; the nonpositive-pivot diagnostic is emitted first, while conditioning classification stays threshold-driven through classify_condition_ratio (governed by D-04).
A nonpositive pivot count greater than zero yields a Warning diagnostic stating the reduced stiffness is not positive definite, located at the first nonpositive pivot.
tolerance_policy_tbd_diagnostic emits a Warning TolerancePolicyTbd diagnostic stating the solver tolerance policy remains TBD and must be accepted before release-quality performance claims.

diagnostic_class_for classifies SparseSolverTbd/TolerancePolicyTbd as Tbd, SolverIteration NonConvergence warnings as NonlinearWarning, IllConditionedSystem as AssumptionWarning, blocking/failure severities as SolveBlocking, and otherwise AssumptionWarning.
default_remediation provides code-specific remediation guidance, including binding the live solve path to the DEC-023 in-repo sparse skyline solver before external performance reliance.
support_finding_diagnostic_code maps every SupportFindingCode variant to SolverDiagnosticCode::InvalidRestraint.

load_finding_diagnostic_code maps load findings either to InvalidNumericInput (magnitude/dimension/direction/property issues) or to InvalidModelTopology (missing IDs/targets, out-of-range, connectivity issues).
load_finding_affected_ref returns 'load:<missing-id>' when the load ID is missing or blank, otherwise the load's own ID.
Unit test module (#[cfg(test)]) for solver diagnostics; verification scaffolding, not a substantive domain claim.
Test confirms a singular frame error maps to a SolveFailed report with a blocking SingularSystem Failure diagnostic sourced from mechanics_solver and provenance location 'core/solver/diagnostics'.
Test confirms sparse_solver_tbd_diagnostic is a non-blocking Warning with analysis-boundary class TBD, not a Failure.
Test confirms the sparse solver diagnostic message references DEC-023, core/solver/sparse_direct, and 'live solve-path adoption remains TBD'.
Test confirms SolverStatus maps to analysis boundary status without human authority: solved states emit no rule status or human acceptance, and failed states require status evidence references.
The open_pipe_stress_frame_kernel crate is described as a code-neutral 3D frame stiffness kernel for OpenPipeStress.
Cargo package metadata (name, version 0.1.0, edition 2021, publish=false, lib path) for the frame kernel crate.

The frame kernel crate is the conservative first slice for DEL-04-01, providing a code-neutral mechanics kernel for 3D Euler-Bernoulli frame stiffness, coordinate transforms, boundary-condition reduction, global dense assembly, and a temporary dense solve interface.
Frame kernel scope: two-node 3D frame elements with six degrees of freedom per node, plus public node and element DOF mapping helpers for the fixed six-DOF ordering.
The kernel provides local 12-by-12 Euler-Bernoulli stiffness terms for axial, torsion, bending about local y, and bending about local z.

The kernel provides direction-cosine transforms from validated local element axes to global axes, and dense global assembly with boundary-condition reduction including force adjustment for prescribed displacements.
The kernel uses deterministic dense Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting for small reduced systems.
Each node uses the deterministic six-DOF ordering [ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz].

For an element, node i occupies DOF indices 0..6 and node j occupies indices 6..12; external slices should bind this ordering via node_dof_index, element_dof_map, FrameDof, and NODE_DOF_ORDER rather than re-deriving offsets.

The dense matrix and dense solve functions are interim interfaces suitable only for focused kernel verification and small tests; the project sparse solver strategy is resolved by DEC-023 as the in-repo skyline LDL^T direct solver, with the dense path serving as the parity oracle. This crate introduces no external numerical dependency.

Inputs to the crate are numeric mechanics quantities that upstream schema and unit layers must already have validated for unit compatibility; the crate validates finite, positive, nondegenerate, orientation, node-index, boundary-condition, and singular-system conditions but does not define the project unit catalog, conversion constants, or solver tolerance policy.
The dense solve path has an internal zero-pivot guard for temporary verification behavior; that guard is not a release tolerance policy, conditioning policy, or sparse-solver selection.

Solver-facing external boundaries must bind raw mechanics fields to FrameKernelUnitBasis metadata before schema, service, adapter, report, or persistence use; the unit basis carries caller-supplied unit identifiers for length, force, moment, stress, area, second_moment_area, displacement, and rotation, performs no conversion, and supplies no defaults.
Optional CanonicalModelReference records bind solver object references to PKG-02 model roles without changing the mechanics kernel.

The shared CanonicalDimension metadata vocabulary exposes force_per_length for downstream solver/load boundaries labeling distributed mechanics quantities; the frame kernel records the dimension identifier only and defines no unit catalog, conversion constants, load defaults, or tolerance policy.

Non-compliance boundary: the frame kernel computes open mechanics quantities only and does not encode compliance rules, code-specific values, protected standard content, material allowables, SIF/flexibility data, private project data, or engineering approval/certification claims.

Frame kernel verification: unit tests cover six-DOF mapping, local stiffness terms, local-to-global transform behavior, global assembly, boundary-condition reduction, prescribed-displacement force adjustment, the temporary dense solve interface, singular-system detection, metadata boundaries, invalid node topology, repeated restraints, invalid orientation, and non-finite input rejection.

The intended future replacement boundary is the reduced-system solve interface; element stiffness, transforms, assembly, and reduction can be preserved while replacing solve_dense with an accepted sparse solver adapter.
The frame kernel crate contains open mechanics routines only; it does not encode design-code compliance checks, protected standards content, or private project data.
Frame kernel DOF constants: DOF_PER_NODE=6, NODES_PER_ELEMENT=2, ELEMENT_DOF=12, with local DOF indices UX=0, UY=1, UZ=2, RX=3, RY=4, RZ=5.
AXIS_TOLERANCE is 1.0e-12; DENSE_SOLVE_ZERO_PIVOT_GUARD is 1.0e-12 and is an internal dense verification pivot guard, not the project solver tolerance policy.
Frame kernel type aliases: Matrix3 is 3x3, Matrix12 is ELEMENT_DOF x ELEMENT_DOF, DenseMatrix is Vec<Vec<f64>>, DenseVector is Vec<f64>.
FrameDof enum names the six local degrees of freedom Ux, Uy, Uz, Rx, Ry, Rz, with local_index, as_str, and is_translational helpers.
FrameDof::is_translational is true for Ux, Uy, and Uz.
NODE_DOF_ORDER is the fixed array [Ux, Uy, Uz, Rx, Ry, Rz] of length DOF_PER_NODE.
node_dof_index computes a global DOF index as node_index * DOF_PER_NODE + dof.local_index().
element_dof_map returns the 12-entry global DOF index map for an element, with node i in the first six entries and node j in the next six.

CanonicalDimension enum enumerates the shared metadata dimension vocabulary including length, force, moment, pressure, stress, area, linear_stiffness, rotational_stiffness, displacement, second_moment_area, force_per_length, slope, and TBD.
CanonicalDimension::as_str returns the canonical string identifier for each dimension (e.g. LinearStiffness -> 'linear_stiffness', Tbd -> 'TBD').
UnitSystemRef wraps a non-empty, non-TBD unit_system_id; its constructor returns None for blank or 'TBD' values.
QuantityUnitMetadata pairs a normalized unit_id with a CanonicalDimension and exposes dimension_id.
FrameKernelUnitBasis binds a unit system reference plus unit metadata for coordinate, force, moment, stress, area, second_moment_area, displacement, and rotation quantities.
FrameKernelUnitBasis::new accepts the unit basis only if has_expected_dimensions passes, ensuring each unit's CanonicalDimension matches its expected role.

FrameKernelUnitBasis::from_unit_ids constructs the basis from string unit IDs, attaching the expected CanonicalDimension to each (length, force, moment, stress, area, second_moment_area, displacement, rotation).
FrameKernelUnitBasis::has_expected_dimensions verifies each unit's dimension equals its required canonical dimension.
CanonicalModelRole enum distinguishes PhysicalSourceOfTruth from AnalyticalSolverModel, with string forms 'physical_source_of_truth' and 'analytical_solver_model'.
CanonicalModelReference binds a model_id, model_role, and object_ref; its constructor rejects blank or TBD identifiers.
normalize_explicit_id trims a value and returns None if it is empty or case-insensitively equal to 'TBD', otherwise the trimmed string.

FrameKernelError enum enumerates validation failures: NonFiniteInput, NonPositiveInput, DegenerateAxis, InvalidOrientation, InvalidNodeIndex, RepeatedElementNodeIndex, InvalidMatrixDimensions, InvalidVectorLength, RepeatedRestrainedDof, RestrainedDofOutOfRange, RepeatedPrescribedDof, PrescribedDofOutOfRange, and SingularSystem.
FrameNode holds an index and 3D coordinates; its constructor validates that coordinates are finite.
FrameSection holds elastic_modulus, shear_modulus, area, second_moment_y, second_moment_z, and torsion_constant; its constructor requires all to be positive and finite.
FrameProperties pairs a FrameSection with a positive finite length.
FrameOrientation stores local unit axes (rows x, y, z) expressed in global coordinates.
FrameOrientation::new validates each axis is finite and unit length, requires mutual orthogonality within AXIS_TOLERANCE, and requires a right-handed basis (cross(x,y) equals z).
FrameOrientation::from_x_axis_and_y_reference builds an orthonormal basis by normalizing the local x axis, Gram-Schmidt projecting the y reference, and taking z as the cross product.
FrameOrientation::transformation_matrix builds a 12x12 transform by copying the 3x3 rotation block onto each node's translational and rotational DOF blocks.
FrameElement holds node_i, node_j, section, and a y_reference vector; its constructor rejects an element connecting a node to itself and validates properties and orientation.
FrameElement::length returns the Euclidean distance between node coordinates (after validating the direction is non-degenerate).
FrameElement::local_stiffness and global_stiffness compute the element local stiffness and then transform it to global coordinates via the element orientation.
ReducedSystem holds the reduced stiffness matrix, reduced force vector, and the list of free (unconstrained) DOFs.
local_stiffness computes the 12x12 Euler-Bernoulli element stiffness: axial = E*A/L, torsion = G*J/L, and bending terms 12EI/L^3, 6EI/L^2, 4EI/L, 2EI/L for both local y and z.
transform_global_stiffness applies T^T * K_local * T using the orientation's transformation matrix.
assemble_global_stiffness builds the dense global stiffness by validating node indices and scattering each element's global stiffness through its element DOF map.
reduce_system constrains the given restrained DOFs to zero displacement and returns the reduced system.
reduce_system_with_prescribed_displacements reduces the system for prescribed (possibly nonzero) boundary displacements.

reduce_system_for_boundary validates a square stiffness matrix and matching finite force vector, rejects out-of-range or repeated boundary DOFs, and adjusts free-DOF forces by subtracting stiffness contributions of prescribed displacements.
The open_pipe_stress_linear_supports crate is described as linear support and restraint models for OpenPipeStress and depends on open_pipe_stress_frame_kernel.
Cargo package metadata (name, version 0.1.0, edition 2021, publish=false, lib path) for the linear supports crate.
The linear supports crate is the bounded implementation slice for DEL-04-03, modeling linear supports and restraints as explicit mechanics-boundary inputs for the 3D frame-kernel DOF order.

The crate covers anchors, guides, line stops, vertical supports, springs, and imposed displacement boundary data; it does not implement nonlinear gap, lift-off, one-way, friction, or active-set behavior, which remain assigned to DEL-04-04.

Linear support inputs are explicit model values that upstream schema and unit layers must validate for unit compatibility; unit-bearing values retain dimension intent such as translational stiffness, rotational stiffness, displacement, or rotation.

SupportQuantity maps dimension intent onto accepted PKG-02 canonical dimensions linear_stiffness, rotational_stiffness, displacement, and rotation, carrying caller-supplied unit identifiers while recording metadata only and performing no conversion or defaulting.
Missing solve-required support data produces deterministic findings rather than silent defaults.

The crate prepares restrained DOFs, linear spring entries, and imposed displacement entries; FrameDof is re-exported from the frame kernel and support DOF indices use the frame-kernel node_dof_index boundary instead of re-derived offsets.

apply_linear_supports validates the dense global system through the frame kernel, adds prepared spring stiffness to global diagonals, and reduces rigid restraints plus imposed displacements through the frame-kernel prescribed displacement boundary.
The linear supports crate does not alter the frame-kernel solver, select a sparse solver, perform load-case algebra, run rule-pack checks, or make professional/code-compliance claims.

Linear supports unit tests cover support-family DOF mapping, missing-data findings, duplicate restraint findings, spring and imposed-displacement validation, and deterministic boundary preparation/application.

The linear supports crate prepares explicit linear support data for the frame-kernel DOF boundary; it does not implement nonlinear support behavior, code checks, protected standards content, or professional approval.
SupportFamily enum names the linear support families: Anchor, Guide, LineStop, VerticalSupport, Spring, and ImposedDisplacement.
QuantityDimension enum covers TranslationalStiffness, RotationalStiffness, Displacement, and Rotation, mapping each to its CanonicalDimension.
SupportQuantity holds a finite value, a QuantityDimension, and optional unit-system reference and unit metadata.
SupportQuantity::new validates a finite value; SupportQuantity::positive additionally requires it be positive.
SupportQuantity::with_unit_metadata rejects metadata whose dimension does not match the quantity's expected canonical dimension (UnitDimensionMismatch).
NodeDof pairs a node_index with a FrameDof and computes its global index via the frame-kernel node_dof_index boundary.
LinearSupport holds a support_id, family, node_index, restrained_dofs, optional stiffness, and optional imposed_displacement.
LinearSupport::anchor restrains all six DOFs (Ux, Uy, Uz, Rx, Ry, Rz) at the node.
LinearSupport::guide restrains the supplied translational DOFs at the node.
LinearSupport::line_stop restrains a single specified DOF at the node.
LinearSupport::vertical_support restrains the Uz DOF at the node.
LinearSupport::spring records a single DOF and optional stiffness quantity for a spring support.
LinearSupport::imposed_displacement records a single DOF and an optional imposed displacement/rotation quantity.
SpringEntry binds a support_id, NodeDof, and a stiffness SupportQuantity; ImposedDisplacementEntry binds a support_id, NodeDof, and a displacement SupportQuantity.

FindingCode enum enumerates support findings: MissingSupportDof, MissingSupportStiffness, MissingImposedDisplacement, InvalidSupportDof, InvalidSupportDimension, RepeatedRestrainedDof, and NodeOutOfRange.
SupportFinding carries a FindingCode, support_id, and message.
BoundaryPreparation holds restrained_dofs, springs, imposed_displacements, and findings; is_blocked is true when any findings are present.
SupportApplication holds the prepared boundary, the spring-augmented stiffness matrix, prescribed DOFs, prescribed displacements, and the reduced system.
LinearSupportError enum covers NonFiniteInput, NonPositiveInput, and UnitDimensionMismatch.
SupportApplicationError enum covers FrameKernel wrapping, BlockingSupportFindings, DofCountNotNodeAligned, SupportDofOutOfRange, and PreparedBoundaryMismatch.

prepare_boundary iterates supports, records a NodeOutOfRange finding when node_index exceeds node_count, dispatches by family to rigid/spring/imposed preparation, and returns sorted restrained DOFs with springs, imposed displacements, and findings.

apply_linear_supports validates the global system, requires the total DOF count be divisible by DOF_PER_NODE, prepares the boundary (blocking on findings), adds spring stiffness to global diagonals, and reduces the system with prescribed displacements.
validate_global_system reduces the system with empty boundary DOFs through the frame kernel and returns the free-DOF count as the total DOF count.
prescribed_displacements_for_boundary maps each imposed displacement onto its prescribed-DOF position, returning PreparedBoundaryMismatch if the DOF is absent.
prepare_rigid_support records MissingSupportDof when no DOFs are given and InvalidSupportDof when a DOF is not allowed for the family, otherwise adding restrained DOFs.
prepare_spring requires one affected DOF and explicit stiffness, and requires the stiffness dimension to match a translational or rotational DOF; otherwise it records a finding.
prepare_imposed_displacement requires one DOF and explicit displacement/rotation whose dimension matches the DOF, then restrains the DOF and records the imposed displacement entry.
add_restrained_dof records a RepeatedRestrainedDof finding if the global DOF is already restrained, otherwise appends it.
dof_allowed_for_family: Anchor allows any DOF; Guide and LineStop allow only translational DOFs; VerticalSupport allows only Uz; Spring and ImposedDisplacement allow any DOF.
dimension_matches_dof requires translational stiffness/displacement for translational DOFs and rotational stiffness/rotation for rotational DOFs.
Test confirms FrameDof re-export matches the frame-kernel boundary and that NODE_DOF_ORDER equals [Ux, Uy, Uz, Rx, Ry, Rz].
Test confirms an anchor at node 1 maps to global restrained DOFs [6,7,8,9,10,11] with no springs.
Test confirms application adds spring stiffness to the global diagonal without mutating the caller's original stiffness matrix.
The open_pipe_stress_nonlinear_supports crate is described as nonlinear support active-set mechanics for OpenPipeStress and depends on linear_supports and solver diagnostics.
Cargo package metadata (name, version 0.1.0, edition 2021, publish=false, lib path) for the nonlinear supports crate.
The nonlinear supports crate is the bounded implementation slice for DEL-04-04, modeling the active-set decision boundary for one-way supports, gaps, lift-off/contact, and friction-limited supports.

The crate consumes trial displacement and reaction facts from a mechanics solve iteration and classifies nonlinear support states as active, inactive, sticking, or sliding, recording changed states, residuals, convergence, and nonconvergence diagnostics.

ActiveSetReportRecord exposes report-facing iteration settings, support states, changed supports, diagnostics, assumptions, and limitations without requiring downstream reports to parse diagnostic text.

The nonlinear supports crate does not assemble or solve the global nonlinear system, select sparse solvers, define release tolerance policy, perform load-case algebra, run rule-pack checks, or make professional/code-compliance claims.
Nonlinear support behavior is explicit model data with no support/catalog defaults supplied.
Sign conventions are explicit through activation and gap-direction enums rather than hidden assumptions.
Gap clearance and friction coefficient fields are validated at both classification time and constructor time, so public-struct callers cannot accidentally receive zero defaults.
Friction behavior uses user/model supplied coefficient and normal reaction values; no engineering defaults are invented.

NonlinearSupportUnitMetadata binds gap/trial displacement, reaction, and friction coefficient values to caller-supplied unit identifiers using accepted PKG-02 dimensions, recording metadata only without conversion or defaulting.
Nonconvergence and nonlinear missing-data errors are surfaced through the solver diagnostics contract.
Report-facing active-set records copy structured diagnostics and explicit assumptions/limitations while preserving the existing solver iteration record.

Nonlinear supports unit tests cover one-way activation, gap opening/closing, missing gap data, lift-off behavior, friction sticking/sliding/contact-loss/missing-coefficient edges, invalid numeric inputs, active-set convergence, and iteration-limit nonconvergence diagnostics, plus report-record conversion fields.
